messages.subject: Line transects for primate survey
parts:
Hi,
I'm going to do a survey on red colobus in five forests in Tanzania. One of
the main goals is to compare the abundace of populations inhabiting the 5
different forests. The 5 forests vary a lot in size and in 4 of them we'll

walk 2 km line transects from North to South only once. The transects
follow a randomly-placed grid. Between 40 and 60 transects will be walked
in each forest and we expect to have enough observations.

My problem is about the fifth forest, which is extremely small and where
using a similar grid or even a slightly smaller one, we are able to walk

only 14 transects and therefore we are not sure we can get enough
observations. What should we do? Should we walk the transects twice in two
different periods so to grant independency? what would be the best solution
to be able later to compare the data from this forest with the ones from

thank you very much for your help.
Best regards
Alessandro Araldi

messages.author: 1fb54f491646a589
messages.subject: Re: Line transects for primate survey
parts:
Alessandro, repeat walking of lines to increase sample size is perfectly OK=
. There is no need for the data from repeat visits to be independent; you=
could re-walk a line the following day. For estimating encounter rate, yo=
ur sample size will still be 14 lines, but that should be sufficient. In D=
istance, you simply record effort for a given line to be line length multip=
lied by the number of occasions it was walked, and pool the detection dista=
nces. See p294 of the introduction to distance sampling book.

Steve Buckland
